newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar says no decision on selling UMW.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar says no decision on selling UMW.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Wednesday the government has not decided on whether to sell its stake in vehicle concern UMW Holdings Bhd.

He told reporters the government would protect the interest of unitholders of state-owned fund Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) on any decision on UMW. The government's 45 percent stake in UMW is held through PNB.
"The government has not made a decision yet. PNB has a special role. We need to protect its unitholders, we don't deny this," Anwar said after an official function at his ministry.
Last week, Anwar said telecommunications concern Sapura Holdings Sdn Bhd had submitted a proposal to the government to buy a stake in UMW.
But Sapura's move raised the ire of PNB officials who said they were not consulted on the proposed sale.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said his comment on the Sapura bid did not mean any decision has been made.
"I only announced submission of the bid because I was asked. There has been a vast number of submissions to acquire companies owned by PNB.
"Hundreds of companies have made submissions in the past. Hundreds have been turned down, some have been accepted. The government is just looking at it," Anwar said.
UMW makes a wide range of light and heavy equipment for use in the industrial, construction and agricultural sectors.
It also assembles and markets passenger and commercial vehicles, and is the Malaysian distributor of Japanese Toyota vehicles.
